summary: Assertion attribute ordering causes RBAC mismatch in private console access
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that after an ingress upgrade, some users in their private VPC lose access to the Redwood Console. The requests succeed to the edge but are denied by RBAC when mapped roles are empty. Impact: Admins and some service users at Aurelia Systems cannot access the console or start scheduled workers; intermittent but reproducible for ~12% of sessions. Environment: Aurelia private deployment (VPC peered), prod region eu-west-1, using our identity-proxy behind customer-managed ingress. Observed behavior: Inbound SAML assertions / OIDC upstream headers arrive at identity-proxy with the expected role attributes documented in the tenant mapping, but the attribute ordering occasionally changes and a downstream header rewrite strips the attribute value when it appears after a different namespace header. Expected behavior: Identity proxy should parse role attributes regardless of ordering; RBAC should map roles consistently. Business impact: Customer-facing admin operations blocked; requested high-priority investigation and temporary mitigation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer-provided test tenant in Aurelia private VPC
2) Initiate SAML SSO login via customer IDP with role attribute set in assertion (roles: admin,devops)
3) Repeat login while toggling ingress rewrite module (http2-to-http1 conversion enabled)
4) Observe identity-proxy request headers and console access outcome

investigation_notes: Initial triage showed the identity-proxy receives a header H: X-Redwood-Roles. In successful flows the header arrives before X-Tenant-Meta; in failing flows the order is reversed. Our header-merge code in the ingress conversion path performs an efficient concatenation but uses a regex that can drop header values when a subsequent header with a similar prefix is present. Reproduced this with an http2-to-http1 conversion case where multiple pseudo-headers are collapsed. Hypothesis: ingress rewrite rule and proxy header normalization interact producing a zero-length value for X-Redwood-Roles when ordering is reversed. Also observed that some client libraries in the customer's on-prem rewrite strips trailing null bytes which amplify the issue.
mitigation_and_workaround: Applied a targeted ingress patch to preserve original assertion header order for Aurelia's load balancer. In addition, recommended customer to reconfigure IDP to send roles in a namespaced single header (X-Redwood-Roles) rather than multiple headers. Temporary ACL rule added to whitelist known admin service accounts so operational access can continue while fix is being validated.
resolution_plan: 1) Patch ingress header-merge regex to correctly preserve multi-valued headers even when ordering changes (PR opened: identity-proxy#2843). 2) Add unit/integration tests covering http2->http1 conversion cases and header reordering. 3) Release hotfix to private deployments and coordinate scheduled rollout with Aurelia. 4) Post-deploy monitor for 72 hours and validate with customer-provided login sweep.
